card.name: Helper words after a subject in warnings
card.fires_on: Small linking or helper words (be, should, can, with) right after a subject such as physicians, prescribers or a drug name, in warning or precaution sentences. Also the last piece of a brand name that starts a sentence.

modes.label: Should be after clinician
modes.description: The word 'be' after 'Physicians/Prescribers/professionals should' in alert statements.
modes.example: Physicians should<< be>> vigilant for clinical symptoms or signs of CM

modes.description: A helper word such as 'should' or 'can' directly after a drug name as sentence subject.

modes.label: End of brand name
modes.description: The closing piece of a capitalized brand name that begins a warning sentence.
modes.example: 5.4 Hepatotoxicity ICLUS<<IG>> can cause hepatotoxicity, including liver

card.writes: Little clear effect; it mildly suppresses vivid descriptive words like 'daunting' or 'looming'.
card.plain: It fires on the small word that follows the subject of a warning sentence, such as 'should be' after 'physicians'.
